meta.title: Health & Safety - A Year In, Not Starting Again

questions.prompt: How does the Year 2 H&S session differ from Year 1's?
options: It's a brisk refresher with a couple of genuinely new bits - familiarity is the risk now
questions.explanation: It's a brisk refresher with a couple of genuinely new bits - familiarity is the risk now.

questions.prompt: Why do habits like skipping sandbags stop registering in year two?
options: Because you've become familiar - not careless. That's the trap
questions.explanation: These stop registering not because you've become careless, but because you've become familiar.

questions.prompt: Which are 'what slips' examples in year two? Select all that apply.
options: Skipping the risk assessment for a familiar location because 'we've been there before'
Things you'd have flagged in week one but stopped noticing
questions.explanation: Lanyards worn 'most of the time', skipping risk assessments for familiar locations, and things you'd have flagged in week one but stopped noticing are the year-two slips.

questions.prompt: If a session this year is in a different studio or building from last year, what should you do?
options: Wait until an alarm to find out
Assume the evacuation route is the same
Treat it as new information - do not assume it is unchanged
questions.explanation: If your sessions this year use a different studio or building from last year, treat this as new information.

questions.prompt: How has the 'show respect' excuse changed in Year 2?
options: There is now an excuse for everything
A year in, 'I didn't realise' carries less weight than it did in week one
questions.explanation: A year in, 'I didn't realise' carries less weight than it did in week one.

questions.prompt: What do Content Creation students now do that they didn't in Year 1?
options: Run live media (Eastbourne Youth Radio, Tag magazine) - with contributor consent and editorial duty of care
questions.explanation: Content Creation students are now running live media - broadcasting and publishing carry different H&S obligations.

questions.prompt: If you are the last person using a piece of equipment, who is responsible for returning it?
options: Whoever signed it out first that day
You - regardless of who signed it out
questions.explanation: If you are the last person using something, you are responsible for returning it, regardless of who signed it out.

questions.prompt: Beyond physical hazards, what else counts as 'something's not right' to tell someone about?
options: Anything - a space, an activity, or the way someone's behaving towards you or someone else - that's made you feel uncomfortable or unsafe
questions.explanation: If a space, an activity, or the way someone's behaving towards you or someone else has made you feel uncomfortable or unsafe, that counts too.
